wikivoyage.text:
Eat:
Portuguese cuisine evolved from hearty peasant food drawn from the land and abundant seafood found in the country's lengthy coast with the cows, pigs and goats raised on the limited grazing land of its interior. From these humble origins, spices and condiments brought back to the country during the exploration and colonisation of South America, Africa, the East Indies and the Far East, contributed to the development of what become regarded as 'typical' Portuguese cuisine which inherently, also helped shape the cuisine in the regions under Portuguese influence, from Brazil and Cape Verde to Thailand and Japan. Today, traditional Portuguese cuisine is served alongside the latest trendy and fusion cuisine styles. Several establishments have been awarded Michelin stars.

Soup is an essential first course of a Portuguese meal. The most popular is the Minho speciality, caldo verde, made from kale, potatoes and spiced smoked sausage.

You will see another Portuguese staple bacalhau (salt cod) everywhere. Locals will tell you that there are as many ways to cook this revered dish as there are days in the year, or even more.

The most common of Portugal's delicious fish (peixe) dishes revolve around sole (linguado) and sardines (sardinha) although salmon (salmão) and trout (truta) are also featured heavily, not mentioning the more traditional mackerel (carapau), whiting (pescada), rock bass (robalo), tuna (atum), frog fish (tamboril) and a variety of turbot (cherne).

In most places you will easily find fresh seafood: lobster (lagosta), crab (caranguejo), lavagante, mussels (mexilhões), cockles (vieiras), oysters (ostras), clam (amêijoas), goose barnacles (perceves).

A peculiarity of Portuguese cuisine is the love of rice and rice-based dishes and desserts, a fondness perhaps grown from the Portuguese travels to the East. Among the most popular rice dishes are "Arroz à Bulhão Pato", essentially a juicy rice and clam dish. Another famous rice dish, "Arroz de Cabidela" consisting of a saucy dish made with rice, chicken and its blood. Besides those already mentioned, there are many varieties of rice-based specialities, such as frog fish rice, octopus rice, duck rice and seafood rice.

Depending on how touristy the area you are in, you'll see grills, thick with the smoke of charring meat, in front of many restaurants during your stay. Other than traditional sardines, Portuguese grilled chicken -- marinated in chilli, garlic and olive oil -- is world famous, althou…

response.text:
See:
Lisbon is a city on the water—the River Tagus (Rio Tejo)—built on seven hills that are traversed by trams. This has led to comparisons with San Francisco. To provide access from the southern suburbs, Lisbon has two spectacular bridges. The 25th of April Bridge (Ponte 25 de Abril) combines the design of the San Francisco–Oakland Bay Bridge with the color of the Golden Gate Bridge, and it's often mistaken for the latter. The Vasco da Gama Bridge (Ponte Vasco da Gama), Europe's longest, was built in the 1990s for Expo '98. One of Lisbon's great landmarks, Cristo Rei, a 28 m statue of Christ the King on an 82 m pedestal, isn't even in Lisbon itself, but across the river in Almada, big enough to be easily seen from the capital.

Alfama:
Built on the hills east of the Baixa, Alfama survived the Great 1755 Earthquake largely intact. Climbing the narrow ancient lanes provides an excellent workout. You can spare your legs by taking the little historic yellow trams that serve the neighborhood. Major sights include Lisbon Cathedral and St. George's Castle.

Bairro Alto:
The Bairro Alto, or "Upper District" (dare we say "High Neighbourhood"), has become Lisbon's youthful, trendy quarter. The district includes the Chiado neighbourhood, known for its numerous historic landmarks and theatres. Among the district's many sights are the São Bento Palace (where the Portuguese parliament meets), the Museu Nacional de Arte Antiga (a museum of antique art), and the Lisbon Botanical Gardens.

response.text:
Eat:
Portuguese dining rituals tend to follow the Mediterranean siesta body clock. Most restaurants are very small, family-run and generally inexpensive. Some of them have a sheet on the door with the pratos do dia (dishes of the day) written on it – these dishes are usually cheaper and fresher than the rest of menu there, and unless you're looking for something specific, they're the right choice. During the dinner the waiter will probably bring you some unrequested starter dishes (called couvert); as those are not free, don't feel obliged to touch them and they will not be charged on your bill (but check it!).

Traditional Portuguese restaurants are in Bairro Alto, scattered abundantly through its quirky narrow streets, and for Portuguese traditional cuisine at its finest, head to the area of Chiado. Tour groups primarily feel at home in Alfama. Tourist traps with laminated menus and meal deals are mostly concentrated in the Baixa area; one exception to this is the Rua das Portas de Santo Antão, a 'seafood strip' northeast from and parallel to Praça dos Restauradores. If you feel like eating with the local people, try the Castelo neighborhood, the smaller family run places serve a fixed daily menu and are not expensive, getting up there by foot will open an appetite, or else go in the elétrico. For a familiar taste at one of the many chain eateries, head to Doca de Santo Amaro (train/tram 15 station Alcantara-Mar) and Parque das Nações (metro Oriental). All the culinary and …

results.name: Leitaria Camponeza
results.summary: On the location of a historical café (the leitaria), this place focuses on only a short number of dishes (meats, fish and seafood) but makes up for this in quality and portion size. For an atmospheric presentation ask for one of their espetadas. The wines complement the dishes and you can end the meal with a dessert. For someone looking for great value for their buck (no compromises on quality), it's a good place to start or end an evening. Price: €15-30

results.name: Mercado da Praça da Figueira
results.summary: From the pavement looks like a small convenience shop, on walking in you realize the deception when confronted by the large cavernous meandering interior space, replete with everything expected from a well stocked supermarket. Although there isn't a restaurant as such, the ready to eat items on offer are tasty, fresh, inexpensive and varied. The sandwiches and hamburgers are superb.

results.name: Mercado Oriental
results.summary: A food court serving Asian street food and the only place in Lisbon where you can try Macanese cuisine (at a stall called "Taberna Macau"). Price: Small dishes €3

results.name: Néctar WineBar
results.summary: A place dedicated to the promotion of Portugal's wine and gastronomic culture, and featuring a daily lunch menu of Portuguese and Mediterranean cuisine. The wine list comprises – in its vast majority – a selection of Portuguese wines which best represent the country. Wine can be bought by the glass, and it is served at the appropriate temperatures and in suitable glasses. Dishes – served in portions for 2 – easily replace a main course meal. results.title: São Jorge Castle
results.extract: São Jorge Castle (Portuguese: Castelo de São Jorge; Portuguese pronunciation: [kɐʃˈtɛlu dɨ sɐ̃w̃ ˈʒɔɾʒɨ]), sometimes known in English as Saint George's Castle, is a historic castle in the Portuguese capital of Lisbon, located in the freguesia of Santa Maria Maior. Human occupation of the castle hill dates to at least the 8th century BC while the oldest fortifications on the site date from the 2nd century BC. The hill on which Saint George's Castle stands has played an important part in the history of Lisbon, having served as the location of fortifications occupied successively by Phoenicians, Carthaginians, Romans, and Moors, before its conquest by the Portuguese in the 1147 Siege of Lisbon. Since the 12th century, the castle has variously served as a royal palace, a military barracks, home of the Torre do Tombo National Archive, and now as a national monument and museum.

results.name: Miradouro de Santa Luzia
results.summary: Good viewpoint in Alfama uphill from the cathedral along tram route. Lovely view over rooftops and river.

results.name: Miradouro da Senhora do Monte
results.summary: The highest viewpoint in Lisbon, at the top of the Graça hill, spread out in front of the small Capela de Nossa Senhora do Monte (founded in 1147, remodelled in the 20th century). To the south you look down over the Castelo de São Jorge, the Mouraria and the Baixa to the Tagus estuary; to the west, from Bairro Alto out to the Monsanto forest; to the north, down the Avenida Almirante Reis valley. It sits a little further out than the viewpoints at Santa Luzia and Portas do Sol, so it is usually quieter, and it is a fine place to watch the sunset.

results.name: Castelo de São Jorge
results.summary: Humans settled on this hill as early as the 8th century BCE, and the first fortifications date from the 1st century BCE. Before the Portuguese conquest in the 1147 Siege of Lisbon, the site was successively occupied by the Phoenicians, Carthaginians, Romans, and Moors. Sights within the castle include the permanent exhibition of archaeological artefacts with an emphasis on the 11th- and 12th-century Moors, ruins of the former Royal Palace of Alcáçova, a garden with native forest species, and a camera obscura showing the city's sights. The castle offers great view over the city and the river. I

results.name: Igreja e Mosteiro de São Vicente de Fora
results.summary: Started in 1582, this Mannerist monastery wasn't completed until 1629, following the reconstruction of a 1147 church under royal decree. The church houses the Pantheon of the House of Braganza, where many monarchs, consorts, and their offspring are entombed.

results.name: Lisbon Cathedral
results.summary: Built in 1147, the cathedral has survived various earthquakes and has undergone restoration, renovation, and modification over the years. Its elements include Romanesque, Gothic, and Baroque styles. It has been a national monument since 1910. Price: , children 7–12 , children 6 & under free

results.name: Museu Nacional do Azulejo
results.summary: One of the most important national museums, dedicated to Portuguese azulejo tiles since the late 1400s. It's in the former Madre de Deus Convent, founded in 1509 by Queen Leonor. Price: , seniors 65+/students/youth card , disabled & children 12 and under free

results.name: Museu Militar de Lisboa
results.summary: Housed in a 16th-century foundry, this museum holds its testaments to Portuguese military history, and contains many artifacts, including a sword used by Vasco da Gama.

results.name: Museu de Sociedade de Geografia
results.summary: Exhibits of ethnography from Portugal's former colonies. Price: , seniors 65+ , students & youths , families of 4 or more  each, disabled & children 12 and under free

results.name: Museu do Teatro Romano
results.summary: Along the way from downtown to Saint George's Castle.

results.name: Panteão Nacional
results.summary: This is one of the most striking buildings in Lisbon. Its tall dome and white facade makes it a real landmark in Alfama/Eastern Lisbon. Excellent views from the rooftop terrace. Construction began in 1681, then halted until the dome was added in 1966 and then converted to the National Pantheon. Amália Rodrigues, queen of fado, is buried here, and fresh roses can be seen on the tomb. The church also has wide viewing platform on the rooftop all around its dome. Excellent panorama of the river and surroundings. No elevator.
results.hours: Tue-Sun 10:00-17:00, platform 10:00-18:00 (closed Mondays, shorter hours in winter)

response.answer: Bacalhau à brás is a traditional Portuguese dish made with shredded salt cod, onions, and thinly fried potato matchsticks, all bound with eggs. The dish is usually garnished with black olives and fresh cilantro or parsley. The main ingredients include salt cod, potatoes, eggs, and onion. The origin of the recipe is uncertain, but it is said to have originated in the late 19th century in Bairro Alto, Lisbon. The name "à brás" is believed to come from a 19th-century Lisbon tavern or restaurant called Braz. The dish is typically served with a side of boiled or steamed veggies or a fresh salad, crusty bread, and a dry white wine like Vinho verde.

We have to produce the merged comparison as per instructions. Need to compute cheapest and fastest for outbound and return among both flight and bus options.

First gather outbound options:

Flight outbound options (5):

1. Ryanair/easyJet: depart 23:15 10 May, arrive 09:55 11 May, duration 760 min, stops 1, price 293.0, details mention airport change (STN→LTN). That's a warning.

2. SAS: depart 11:15, arrive 16:10 same day, duration 415 min, stops 1, price 297.0, no airport change.

3. Norwegian/easyJet: depart 17:45, arrive 23:05 same day, duration 440 min, stops 1, price 340.0, different airlines self-transfer maybe.

4. Ryanair: depart 22:35, arrive 08:50 next day, duration 735 min, price 342.0, no mention of airport change? It seems no change.

5. Finnair: depart 13:00, arrive 15:50 same day, duration 290 min, price 411.0, nonstop.

Ground outbound options (3 bus):

All three have price 353.9 total for 2 travellers. Duration:

- Option 1: duration 5418 min (~90 hrs = 3.75 days), arrival 2027-05-14T07:05 (4 days later). Price 353.9.

- Option 2: duration 4608 min (~76.8 hrs = 3.2 days), arrival 2027-05-13T17:35 (3.3 days later). Price same 353.9.

- Option 3: duration 5187 min (~86.45 hrs), arrival 2027-05-14T07:05 (same as option 1). Price same.

All have no warnings about airport change; they are bus to Lisbon.

Cheapest outbound: need lowest price_eur among all. Flight cheapest is 293.0 (Ryanair/easyJet). Bus cheapest is 353.9. So cheapest is flight option 1 at €293.0.

Fastest outbound: lowest duration_min. Compare:

- Flight: durations: 290 (Finnair), 415 (SAS), 440 (Norwegian/easyJet), 735, 760.

- Bus: min 4608.

Thus fastest is Finnair direct flight, 290 min, price 411.0.

Now need to rank up to 5 best value options, sorting by price, but move down if much slower (>2x fastest) or has airport change warning.

Fastest is 290 min; 2x fastest = 580 min. So any option >580 minutes considered much slower. That includes flights of 735, 760; also all buses (4608 etc). Also flight with duration 440 still within 580, okay.

Now we need to sort by price (lowest to highest) but adjust for warnings.

List all options with price and warnings:

A) Ryanair/easyJet (price 293, duration 760, warning airport change). Duration > 580, also warning.

B) SAS (price 297, duration 415, no warning, within 580)

C) Norwegian/easyJet (price 340, duration 440, warning self-transfer but not explicit airport change; still possible. It says "different airlines: possibly a self-transfer". That qualifies as "self-transfer" warning, rule says move down when details warn about self-transfer or airport change.

D) Ryanair (price 342, duration 735, no warning but duration >580.

E) Finnair (price 411, duration 290, no warning, fastest.

Bus options: price 353.9 each, duration >4600, no airport warning but far slower, >2x fastest, so should be moved down.

Ranking priority: start with cheapest price but adjust.

Let's order by price:

1) Ryanair/easyJet (293) but has airport change and duration >580 => move down maybe after some higher priced but better.

2) SAS (297) good.

3) Norwegian/easyJet (340) warning self-transfer and duration acceptable.

4) Ryanair (342) duration >580 but no warning.

5) Bus (353.9) far slower.

6) Finnair (411) expensive but fastest.

We need up to 5 options; include the best value ones. Considering adjustments, maybe order:

- SAS (good price, decent duration, no warning) => rank 1.

- Norwegian/easyJet (price 340, some self-transfer warning) => rank 2.

- Ryanair (price 342, long duration) => rank 3.

- Bus (price 353.9) but very long => rank 4.

- Finnair (price 411, fastest) => rank 5 (maybe after bus? but price higher, but faster; rule says move down when much slower; bus is much slower, so bus should be after Finnair maybe? Actually bus is much slower, so should be moved down relative to faster options. So Finnair should be above bus despite higher price.)

Thus final ranking: SAS, Norwegian/easyJet, Ryanair (342), Finnair (411), Bus (353.9)??? But bus cheaper than Finnair, yet far slower. Rule: move down when >2x fastest. So we should place Finnair before bus, even though price higher. So ranking could be:

1. SAS (297)

2. Norwegian/easyJet (340) (self-transfer warning but still okay)

3. Ryanair (342) (long duration but no warning)

4. Finnair (411) (fastest)

5. Bus (353.9) (very long, moved down despite cheaper price)

But note bus price is 353.9 < 411, but we moved it down due to slowness.

We also need to consider Ryanair/easyJet at 293 but has airport change and long duration; probably should be after Ryanair 342? Since warning and long. So maybe exclude it from top 5? But we have only 5 slots; we already have 5. However we could choose to include Ryanair/easyJet as 5th and drop bus; but bus cheaper. Let's evaluate: which is better value? Bus is cheap but extremely slow; Ryanair also slow and with airport change. Both have issues. Maybe keep bus because price lower than Finnair and Ryanair has no warning but is still long. However bus is 5 days total, while Ryanair 760 min (12h) plus airport change (transfer time not counted). Actually Ryanair duration 760 min (12h 40m). That's less than 24h; bus is 4 days. So Ryanair less slow. So ranking should favor Ryanair over bus. So maybe we keep Ryanair and drop bus from top 5 (since we have only 5). But we need up to 5; we have 6 candidates (including Ryanair/easyJet). We could choose 5 best after adjusting. Probably drop the worst (bus) because it's extremely slow.

Thus ranked list: SAS, Norwegian/easyJet, Ryanair (342), Finnair, Ryanair/easyJet (airport change) maybe? Let's re-evaluate.

List all with adjusted ranks:

- SAS (297) best.

- Norwegian/easyJet (340) (self-transfer warning) moderate.

- Ryanair (342) (no warning) longer duration but still okay.

- Finnair (411) fastest but more expensive.

- Ryanair/easyJet (293) cheapest but airport change and very long; may be placed last.

That gives 5 ranked options.

Now Return options:

Flight return 5 options:

1. Ryanair,SAS: depart 06:50, arrive 20:25, duration 695, stops 2, price 283.0, warning: different airlines, possibly self-transfer; includes airport change? It says different airlines, possible self-transfer but not explicit airport change.

2. TAP Portugal,SAS: price 355.0, duration 655, stops 2, warning same as above (self-transfer).

3. easyJet,Norwegian: price 382.0, duration 605, stops 1, warning self-transfer.

4. Finnair: price 387.0, duration 275, nonstop, no warning.

5. Ryanair,Finnair: price 387.0, duration 590, stops 1, warning airport change (STN→LHR) plus self-transfer.

Ground return options: three bus options price 299.96 each, duration about 4300-4461 min (~71-74 hrs). No warnings.

Cheapest return: find lowest price. Among flights, cheapest is 283.0 (Ryanair,SAS) but has self-transfer warning. Bus price 299.96 each (per 2 travellers total). So cheapest is flight at 283.

Fastest return: lowest duration. Compare durations: Finnair 275 min fastest (nonstop). Next easyJet/Norwegian 605, Ryanair/Finnair 590, others 655, 695. So fastest is Finnair (275), price 387.

Now ranking return up to 5 with adjustments.

List options with price and warnings:

A) Ryanair,SAS (283) duration 695, warnings self-transfer.

B) Bus (299.96) duration ~4300, no warning but very slow.

C) TAP Portugal,SAS (355) duration 655, self-transfer.

D) easyJet/Norwegian (382) duration 605, self-transfer.

E) Finnair (387) duration 275, no warning fastest.

F) Ryanair,Finnair (387) duration 590, airport change warning.

Now we sort by price and adjust for slowness (>2x fastest). Fastest duration = 275. 2x fastest = 550. Options longer than 550 should be moved down (i.e., slower). So durations >550 (605, 590, 655, 695, 4300) all slower, move down. So only Finnair qualifies as fast enough (<550). The bus is far slower, move down.

Thus ranking likely:

1. Finnair (387) best speed, price moderate.

2. Ryanair,SAS (283) cheapest but slow and self-transfer; maybe rank after Finnair due to warning/performance.

3. TAP Portugal,SAS (355) slower, warning.

4. easyJet/Norwegian (382) similar.

5. Bus (299.96) cheaper than some flights but very slow.

We need 5 options; we have them.

Now compute total_cheapest_eur: cheapest outbound (293) + cheapest return (283) = 576.0 EUR.

Now recommendation: Should recommend combination based on mid budget, travellers 2, prefer reasonable time. The bus takes many days, not suitable for 4-night stay; so flights are advisable. For outbound, cheapest is Ryanair/easyJet but has airport change and long duration; the SAS flight is only slightly more expensive and smooth. For return, fastest Finnair nonstop is good albeit more pricey; however total cost still within budget. ## Where to stay

- **Rating**: 4.86/5 (425 reviews)

## Day by day

### Day 1 – Mon 2027-05-10: Alfama

### Day 2 – Tue 2027-05-11: Belém

- **15:30 Monument to the Discoveries** – 1960 monument commemorating the Age of Discovery; climb for sweeping Tagus views. *ticket €4* [source](https://en.wikivoyage.org/wiki/Lisbon/Bel%C3%A9m)
- **19:00 Dinner near Belém** – Casual waterfront dining (seafood grills, petiscos). [no source]

# Lisbon trip guide: 2027-05-10 – 2027-05-14

Two adults travelling from Helsinki on a relaxed, mid‑budget itinerary (total budget **€2500**). Interests are history and street food. The weather information is **typical** for these dates, not a forecast.

## Getting there and back

**Chosen flights**

| Return   | flight | Finnair | 2027‑05‑14 16:35 → 2027‑05‑14 23:10 | 275 min | 0 | €387 (live) | [link](https://kiwi.com/u/td7ff32) |

**Alternative flights**

| Fastest outbound  | flight | Finnair | 2027‑05‑10 13:00 → 2027‑05‑10 15:50 | 290 min | 0 | €411 (live) | [link](https://kiwi.com/u/p663wh) |
| Cheapest return   | flight | Ryanair, SAS | 2027‑05‑14 06:50 → 2027‑05‑14 20:25 | 695 min | 2 | €283 (live) | [link](https://kiwi.com/u/3xgwh26) |
| Fastest return    | flight | Finnair (chosen) | 2027‑05‑14 16:35 → 2027‑05‑14 23:10 | 275 min | 0 | €387 (live) | [link](https://kiwi.com/u/td7ff32) |

**Warnings**
- The cheapest outbound involves an airport change in London (STN → LTN) and requires you to transfer yourself between airports.
- The cheapest return has two stops (Lisbon → AGP → ARN → HEL) and also requires self‑transfer.
- All listed flights include 2 personal items per traveller; no checked bags are included.

## Where to stay

**Chosen accommodation**: **Green View Home** (hotel) – €44 per night, total **€176** (live), rating **4.1/5**. Central location, free Wi‑Fi, kitchen in some rooms, smoke‑free. Chosen for best value and relaxed pace.

| Area | Airbnb | Hotel | From €/night |
|---|---|---|---|
| Alfama | [Alfama Duplex Best river Views in Lisbon](https://www.airbnb.com/rooms/13744951?check_in=2027-05-10&check_out=2027-05-14&adults=2) – €218.5 | [Alfama - Lisbon Lounge Suites (Alojamento Local)](https://www.booking.com/searchresults.html?ss=Alfama+-+Lisbon+Lounge+Suites+%28Alojamento+Local%29%2C+Lisbon&checkin=2027-05-10&checkout=2027-05-14&group_adults=2&no_rooms=1) – €69.75 | €69.75 |
| Centro | [The Restauradores Collection — Regal](https://www.airbnb.com/rooms/1544825059228796071?check_in=2027-05-10&check_out=2027-05-14&adults=2) – €198.5 | [Rossio Plaza Hotel](https://www.booking.com/searchresults.html?ss=Rossio+Plaza+Hotel%2C+Lisbon&checkin=2027-05-10&checkout=2027-05-14&group_adults=2&no_rooms=1) – €109.44 | €109.44 |
| Outskirts | [Villa Tejo II](https://www.airbnb.com/rooms/1751573277720543502?check_in=2027-05-10&check_out=2027-05-14&adults=2) – €127.75 | [Famous Crows Guest House](https://www.booking.com/searchresults.html?ss=Famous+Crows+Guest+House%2C+Lisbon&checkin=2027-05-10&checkout=2027-05-14&group_adults=2&no_rooms=1) – €71.0 | €71.0 |

**Recommendation** – Green View Home offers the cheapest total price while keeping a central position, making it ideal for a relaxed, mid‑budget stay. Note that LiteAPI hotel rates may be slightly below public prices and city tax (€32.59) is not included in the shown total.

## Day by day

*Days in this plan start around 09:30 and end by 22:00, at a relaxed pace. For another rhythm, tell the concierge, e.g. "we wake up early, start at 07:00", "we stay out late" or "a more relaxed pace, please".*

### Day 1 – Mon 2027-05-10: São Jorge Castle & Lisbon Cathedral
**Weather**: light rain, 13‑17 °C (rainy). **Walk**: ~1 km.
- **16:10 Arrive in Lisbon** – Flight with SAS, see *Getting there and back*.
- **16:45 Lisbon Cathedral** – The city’s oldest church, founded in 1147 after the reconquest; blends Romanesque, Gothic and Baroque elements. Open Mon–Sat 10:00‑18:30. *ticket price: see the website* [source](https://en.wikivoyage.org/wiki/Lisbon/Alfama).
- **18:30 São Jorge Castle** – Historic fortress occupied since the 8th century BC; served as royal palace and military barracks. Open Mo‑Su 09:00‑21:00. *ticket price: see the website* [source](https://www.openstreetmap.org/way/1382432568).
- **20:30 Leitaria Camponeza** – Mid‑range dinner, try the grilled fish. Budget tier **mid**. [source](https://en.wikivoyage.org/wiki/Lisbon/Baixa).

### Day 2 – Tue 2027-05-11: Belém (Jerónimos & Discoveries)
**Weather**: drizzle, 13‑18 °C (rainy). **Walk**: ~7 km.
- **10:00 Mosteiro dos Jerónimos** – Manueline masterpiece built in the 16th century, UNESCO World Heritage. Open Tue‑Sun 10:00‑18:30 (May‑Sep). *ticket €18* [source](https://en.wikivoyage.org/wiki/Lisbon/Bel%C3%A9m).
- **12:30 Lunch near Belém** – Sample nearby street‑food stalls, especially pastéis de nata.
- **13:00 Monument to the Discoveries** – 1960 monument shaped like a caravel prow, commemorates the Age of Discovery; climb for views of the Tagus. *ticket €4* [source](https://en.wikivoyage.org/wiki/Lisbon/Bel%C3%A9m).
- **19:00 Mercado Oriental** – Low‑budget Asian street food market, try the Macanese stall. Budget tier **low**. Open 12:00–22:30. [source](https://en.wikivoyage.org/wiki/Lisbon/Baixa).

### Day 3 – Wed 2027-05-12: Eduardo VII Park area
**Weather**: rain, 13‑18 °C (rainy). **Walk**: ~1 km.
- **10:00 Museu Nacional do Desporto** – Museum of Portuguese sport heritage, free entry. Open Tu‑Su 10:00‑17:00. *free entry* [source](https://www.openstreetmap.org/node/5068486966).
- **12:30 Rosa da Rua Restaurante** – Mid‑budget lunch, buffet of Portuguese dishes. Budget tier **mid**. Open Mon‑Fri 12:00‑15:30 & 19:30‑22:30. [source](https://en.wikivoyage.org/wiki/Lisbon/Bairro_Alto).
- **14:00 Monumento aos Restauradores** – Monument commemorating the 1640 Restoration War that ended Spanish rule. *ticket price: see the website* [source](https://opentripmap.com/en/card/W663347630).
- **19:00 Café Buenos Aires** – High‑budget grilled meats, try the steak. Budget tier **high**. Open Mon‑Fri 16:00‑23:00, Sat 12:00‑16:00, closed Sun. [source](https://en.wikivoyage.org/wiki/Lisbon/Bairro_Alto).

### Day 4 – Thu 2027-05-13: Chiado
**Weather**: drizzle, 13‑20 °C (no rain). **Walk**: ~0.7 km.
- **10:00 Museu Nacional de Arte Contemporânea – Museu do Chiado** – Contemporary art collection of Portuguese and international works. Open Tu‑Su 10:00‑18:00. *ticket price: see the website* [source](https://www.openstreetmap.org/way/96321716).
- **12:30 Faca & Garfo** – Grilled Portuguese specials, mids. Budget tier **mid**. Open Mon‑Sat 08:00‑24:00. [source](https://en.wikivoyage.org/wiki/Lisbon/Bairro_Alto).
- **15:00 Museu Nacional do Azulejo** – Tile museum housed in the former Madre de Deus Convent, showcases azulejo art from the 15th century onward. Open Tue‑Sun 10:00‑13:00 & 14:00‑18:00, closed Mon. *ticket price: see the website* [source](https://en.wikivoyage.org/wiki/Lisbon/Alfama).
- **19:00 Alma** – Two‑Michelin‑star fine dining, try the tasting menu. Budget tier **high**. Open Tue‑Sun 12:30‑15:30 & 19:00‑22:30, closed Mon. [source](https://en.wikivoyage.org/wiki/Lisbon/Bairro_Alto).

### Day 5 – Fri 2027-05-14: Gulbenkian
**Weather**: overcast, 13‑20 °C (no rain). **Walk**: ~1.9 km.
- **10:00 Calouste Gulbenkian Museum** – World‑class collection of antiquities, European, Islamic and modern art. Open Su‑Mo, We‑Fr 10:00‑18:00; Sa 10:00‑21:00. *ticket price: see the website* [source](https://www.openstreetmap.org/way/188143627).
- **12:30 Os Tibetanos** – Mid‑budget vegetarian/vegan lunch, try the tofu and juice bar. Budget tier **mid**. Open Mon‑Fri 12:15‑14:45 & 19:30‑22:30, Sat 12:45‑15:30 & 20:00‑23:00. [source](https://en.wikivoyage.org/wiki/Lisbon/Bairro_Alto).
- **16:35 Depart from Lisbon** – Flight with Finnair, see *Getting there and back*.

## Food to try
- **Caldo verde** – Portuguese soup. [source](https://www.wikidata.org/wiki/Q770977)
- **Pastel de nata** – Portuguese egg‑tart pastry dusted with cinnamon. [source](https://www.wikidata.org/wiki/Q1421401)
- **Feijoada** – Bean and meat stew popular in Portuguese‑speaking areas. [source](https://www.wikidata.org/wiki/Q878189)
- **Francesinha** – Portuguese sandwich. [source](https://www.wikidata.org/wiki/Q732)
- **Fios de ovos** – Portuguese egg dessert. [source](https://www.wikidata.org/wiki/Q3275692)
- **Cocido** – Spanish or Portuguese stew. [source](https://www.wikidata.org/wiki/Q868158)

## Cost estimate

| Category | Total (€) | Share |
|---|---|---|
| Transport | 684.0 | 40.6 % |
| Stay | 176.0 | 10.5 % |
| Food | 700.0 | 41.6 % |
| Activities | 44.0 | 2.6 % |
| Local transport | 80.0 | 4.8 % |
| **Total** | **1684.0** | **67.4 %** |

- **Per person**: €842.0
- **Per person per day**: €168.4
- **Budget**: €2500 – within budget (budget used ≈ 67 %).

**Assumptions**
- Food: typical mid‑budget cost of €50 per person per day.
- Local transport: typical €8 per person per day.
- Extra €200 allocated for the planned restaurants that exceed the mid‑budget (low €15, mid €30, high €80 per person).
- Six sights with unknown ticket price counted as €0.

## Good to know
- No source failures; all data retrieved successfully.
- Cheapest outbound and return options involve airport changes and self‑transfers – double‑check logistics.
- Some attractions (e.g., Museu Nacional do Azulejo) are closed on Mondays; plan accordingly.
- City tax for hotels may not be included in the displayed price.
- No major events are listed for the travel dates.
- Before booking, check your government's official travel advice for Portugal (safety, entry rules, insurance).
